title: Unique Substrings in Wraparound String
summary: Define the infinite wraparound string base as '...zabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcd....'.
statement: Define the infinite wraparound string base as '...zabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcd....'. Given a string s, count the distinct non-empty substrings of s that appear in base.
constraints: Count distinct nonempty substring VALUES present in the infinite cyclic alphabet ...xyzabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz...
Consecutive z→a is valid. Repeated occurrences of the same substring count once.
hints: Within the cyclic alphabet, a substring is determined by its final letter and length.
Track the longest valid consecutive run ending at each of the 26 letters.
Extend the run when character differences are 1 modulo 26; otherwise reset to 1. Maximize the record for this final letter.
If the longest run ending at a letter has length L, exactly L distinct lengths are represented for that ending. Sum the 26 maxima.
editorial: All shorter suffixes of a valid run are valid. For a fixed final letter and length there is only one cyclic-alphabet string, so the maximum run length counts distinct values without storing substrings or recounting repeated occurrences. The oracle enumerates a set of substrings and checks membership in a sufficiently long literal cyclic alphabet.

tests.explanation: The only nonempty substring is a, which occurs in the cyclic alphabet.
The six distinct valid substrings are z,a,b,za,ab,zab; z→a crosses the alphabet boundary.
